correctness.rationale: For all positive coefficients with \(r>e\), \(m=c\) and \(\mu=e+p/a-r>0\), sufficiently small positive \(q,\delta\) define an invariant wedge. Prey decays exponentially and predator density satisfies \(y(t)=\Theta(t^{-1/2})\). The exact identity \(d[c/(sy)+c^2/(2sy^2)]/dt=1-nx(y+c)/(y(nx+c))\) has integrable error; inversion gives the two-term predator expansion. The exact logarithmic prey identity yields the fear-modified \(\sqrt t\) exponent, \(\log t\) power and a finite positive normalized limit for every initial point in the wedge. An exact symbolic checker and rational witness were replayed; finite-time diagnostics are not the proof.

value.rationale: The equality \(m=c\) is the natural biological Allee/alternative-food collision, not an arbitrary parameter slice. At this point hyperbolic predator decay fails. On an open set of valid positive initial data, the theorem quantifies both algebraic predator extinction and an unusual fear-induced \(\sqrt t\) modification of exponentially dying prey, including a nontrivial log-power and positive amplitude. These sharp rates affect transient extinction-time calculations and distinguish behavioral fear from baseline predation; not a rephrasing of equilibrium eigenvalues.
